summary: A tiny app-wide **publish/subscribe** channel built on the browser's own `EventTarget`. Modules announce things with `bus.emit(type, payload)` and listen with `bus.on(type, handler)`, which returns an unsubscribe function. It decouples the SSE client (`live.js`), the API layer (`api.js`), the shell (`main.js`) and the pages, which never need references to each other.

notes.text: Header comment: an app-wide pub/sub channel. Pages listen for live events here instead of on the `EventSource` itself, so there is exactly one SSE connection however many listeners exist.

A private `EventTarget`, the browser's built-in event dispatcher (the same machinery DOM elements use), so no library is needed. It is not part of the DOM, so these events never mix with real DOM events.
The exported `bus` object, imported by any module that needs to notify or listen to others without importing them.
`on(type, handler)` wraps the handler so subscribers receive just the payload (`e.detail`) rather than the event object.
Registers the wrapper for that event type.
Returns an **unsubscribe** function that removes exactly this wrapper. `ctx.on()` in `main.js` stores it, which is how a page's listeners are removed when you navigate away.
`emit(type, detail)` dispatches a `CustomEvent` that carries the payload in `detail`. Dispatch is synchronous: every handler has run by the time `emit` returns. The last line closes the `bus` object.
